title: Draw a 50 mm-radius circle with a school compass round a marked cross, holding the loose sheet still
instruction: Draw a circle around the cross with the compass, then set the compass down on the table off the board.
context: Drawing a circle with a pair of compasses is a basic school and homework skill (US Common Core HSG-CO.D.12: geometric constructions with compass and straightedge). One hand holds the loose sheet flat, or the pencil's drag spins it round the needle; the other plants the needle on the centre and moves the grip round it with light, even pressure on the lead. Press hard and the hinge spreads and the line spirals; lift and the line breaks; let the sheet turn and the circle misses its centre.
setup: Table frame, cm: x forward from the arm-base midpoint, y left, z up. Cork board 26 x 32 x 0.3 at (30, -4). On it a loose A4 sheet (21.0 x 29.7, 80 g/m2, 5 g), long side along y, centre (30, -4), printed cross at (27, -11). A school compass (11.5 cm legs, 50 mm preset spread, 44 g, knurled grip sleeve that turns on the stem) stands legs-down in a blue desk-tidy cup (inside 7.4 x 6.0 x 4.0 deep) at (12, -25), legs along x. Both arms start at READY, grippers open.
scoring: Score 0 if the sheet turns > 5 deg or slides > 5 mm at any time. A mark counts only where the lead leaves a line (presses >= 0.15 N) while the needle is pricked in the sheet. 0.3: >= 180 deg of arc round the cross; 0.6: >= 340 deg, every mark 50 +- 2 mm from the cross and the fitted centre within 2 mm of it; 1.0: also no gap > 3 mm, the compass set down on the table >= 1 cm outside the board, needle out, still 1 s, grippers open, >= 10 cm from the compass, >= 5 cm above the sheet if over it, and still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Print the cross (two 12 x 1.5 mm bars) at sheet-local (-3, -7) cm and lay the sheet on the board tape marks (cross at 27, -11 cm). Check the compass spread on a ruler (50 mm needle point to lead) and stand it legs-down on the cup floor, centred at (12, -25), legs along x, needle leg toward -x.
fidelity: Rigid sheet (0.5 mm collider), board, cup and compass at true size. The hinge holds its spread with 10 N m/rad; the sleeve turns on a free bearing. Pressing the needle on the sheet with >= 0.6 N pins its point sideways (prick hole) until it lifts 2 mm out. The pencil line is recorded where the lead presses. Grasp: force-limited pad grip, engages only on two-pad contact with the jaws closed; caps 50 N pull, 0.5 N m twist, 1.5 N m tip; slips above a cap.
